note: One Wikimedia Commons image per laureate showing the prize work itself (artifact, apparatus, structure, diagram, publication or place), not a portrait. Licences read from Commons extmetadata; only public domain, CC0, CC BY and CC BY-SA accepted. Each thumbnail was downloaded and checked visually. width/height are the API thumbwidth/thumbheight for iiurlwidth=640; the served thumb_url can be a 960px bucket or the unscaled original, with the same aspect ratio. Where no relevant licensed image was found the laureate is listed under gaps rather than given a loosely related image.

1.file: File:First medical X-ray by Wilhelm Röntgen of his wife Anna Bertha Ludwig's hand - 18951222.jpg
1.caption_he: "יד עם טבעות": צילום הרנטגן של יד אשתו ברתה, 1895
1.caption_en: "Hand mit Ringen": Röntgen's X-ray of his wife Bertha's hand, 1895
1.relation: One of the first X-ray images, made by Röntgen himself in December 1895 weeks after he discovered the rays the prize honours.

6.file: File:Ionisation chamber made by Pierre Curie, c 1895-1900. (9660571297).jpg
6.artist: Science Museum London / Science and Society Picture Library
6.caption_he: תא יינון שבנה פייר קירי למדידת קרינה רדיואקטיבית
6.caption_en: Ionisation chamber built by Pierre Curie to measure radioactivity
6.relation: Instrument of the kind the Curies used to quantify the radiation of uranium and other substances, the measurements behind the 1903 prize on radiation phenomena.

962.caption_he: סכמת הגברת פולס מצויץ: מתיחה, הגברה ודחיסה (תוויות בצרפתית)
962.caption_en: Chirped pulse amplification scheme: stretch, amplify, compress (French labels)
962.relation: Schematic of the chirped pulse amplification technique itself; a generic diagram, not Strickland's original apparatus.

160.artist: J. H. van 't Hoff; revised by Ernst Cohen; translated by Thomas Ewan
160.caption_he: דף השער של "מחקרים בדינמיקה כימית", מהדורה אנגלית 1896
160.caption_en: Title page of 'Studies in Chemical Dynamics', English edition 1896
160.relation: English edition of van 't Hoff's Études de dynamique chimique (1884), the work on chemical dynamics cited by the prize; page 9 of the scanned book.

230.file: File:Model of the Structure of Penicillin, by Dorothy Hodgkin, Oxford, c.1945.jpeg
230.artist: Museum of the History of Science, University of Oxford
230.caption_he: מודל צפיפות אלקטרונים של פניצילין, מעבודת הודג'קין
230.caption_en: Electron-density contour model of penicillin from Hodgkin's work
230.relation: Three-dimensional electron-density map of penicillin built from the X-ray crystallography by Hodgkin and colleagues that the prize recognises.

292.caption_he: סכמת ניסוי משאבה-גשוש בפולסי אור קצרים
292.caption_en: Schematic of a pump–probe experiment with short light pulses
292.relation: Generic schematic of the pump–probe principle that Zewail's femtosecond spectroscopy used to watch transition states; not his own apparatus.

1055.caption_he: מבנה הגביש של MOF-5: צמתי אבץ מחוברים במקשרים אורגניים
1055.caption_en: Crystal structure of MOF-5: zinc clusters joined by organic linkers
1055.relation: MOF-5, the framework reported by Yaghi's group in 1999, is a canonical example of the metal–organic frameworks cited by the prize; rendering is a modern illustration.

299.file: File:Cajal - a purkinje neuron from the human cerebellum.jpg
299.caption_he: ציור יד של קחאל: תא פורקיניה מהמוח הקטן של האדם
299.caption_en: Cajal's drawing of a Purkinje neuron from the human cerebellum
299.relation: Original drawing by Cajal (Museo Cajal, Madrid) of the nerve-cell structure his prize-winning work described.

428.caption_he: גרגירי תירס בדגם פסיפס מתנועת היסודות Ac/Ds
428.caption_en: Maize kernels with mosaic colour caused by Ac/Ds movement
428.relation: McClintock's own figure showing how Ac/Ds mobile elements produce variegated kernel colour, the evidence for mobile genetic elements.

918.caption_he: לענה חד-שנתית (Artemisia annua), הצמח שממנו הופק ארטמיסינין
918.caption_en: Sweet wormwood (Artemisia annua), the plant source of artemisinin
918.relation: The plant from which Tu Youyou's team extracted artemisinin; photographed in Germany, not at her laboratory.

1024.caption_en: Uridine versus pseudouridine: the nucleoside modification
1024.relation: Shows the uridine-to-pseudouridine substitution, the kind of nucleoside modification Karikó and Weissman found lets mRNA avoid an inflammatory response.

462.caption_he: "זיכרון מסולפרינו" מאת דונאן, מהדורה ראשונה, ג'נבה 1862
462.caption_en: Dunant's 'Un Souvenir de Solferino', first edition, Geneva 1862
462.relation: Dunant's book on the wounded at Solferino, which led to the founding of the Red Cross; copy held by the ICRC Library.

496.relation: The Chicago settlement house Jane Addams co-founded in 1889 and ran, the base of her social and peace work.

809.caption_he: בניין המטה של בנק גראמין, מירפור, דאקה
809.caption_en: Grameen Bank headquarters building, Mirpur, Dhaka
809.relation: Headquarters of the Grameen Bank, the microcredit institution Yunus founded and shared the prize with.

gaps.678: No Commons image of Tinbergen's dynamic econometric models or his 1930s model publications was found; the 'Tinbergen' results are mostly Niko Tinbergen's ethology figures.
gaps.719: Welfare-economics theory has no physical artifact; his books are under copyright and no freely licensed relevant figure was found.
gaps.846: Only portraits and press-conference photos of Ostrom were found. Commons has aerial photos of Törbel (one of her cases) under a Swisstopo attribution licence outside the accepted list, and no licensed image of the commons or irrigation systems she studied was clearly tied to her work.
gaps.1034: Her work is historical labour-market data analysis; no freely licensed image of her figures or data series was found.
gaps.783: Commons has portraits of Maathai and official visits, but no licensed photo of Green Belt Movement tree planting or nurseries was found.
